gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the same defect in defvs: injectivity of retained DoFs on the target serendipity space is incorrectly used to make the L2 projection moments computable for arbitrary v and to establish the resulting reduced-space interface. ISSUE-001 also explicitly recognizes the resulting loss of computability and unisolvence and specifies the required factorization/reconstructibility condition.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The preserved DoFs do not in general determine the L2 right-hand sides against the serendipity space, so the projector and reduced DoFs cannot be recovered from them; consequently the claimed computable and unisolvent serendipity construction and its dependent results are unsupported.

component_coverage.gold_component: The identifying condition does not make the L2 moments (v,p) computable from the preserved DoFs, and therefore does not establish the claimed computable, unisolvent reduced interface or dependent construction.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 directly states that retained-DoF injectivity does not compute the L2-projection right-hand sides, gives the same-data/different-moment manifestation, identifies the failure of computability and unisolvence, and requires reconstructibility of all moments plus unisolvence as the repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries diagnose the failure of the commuting proof to establish that the mapped functions satisfy all reduced serendipity DoFs and therefore belong to the target spaces. ISSUE-002 specifically identifies the omitted interior curl-related, edge, and boundary requirements, the lack of projection compatibility, and the circular use of equality before target-space membership is proved.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The displayed differential identities are not established because checking preserved normal-flux, divergence, or gradient-related data does not verify the reduced target-space DoFs or establish membership in the serendipity spaces; invoking equality from matching DoFs before that membership is known is circular.

component_coverage.gold_component: The curl and gradient commuting identities fail to prove all reduced target-space DoFs and membership, making the membership argument circular and leaving the commuting diagram and dependent estimates unproved.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies the checked versus un checked DoFs for the identities, the missing compatibility between the relevant L2 projections and reduced spaces, the additional order hypotheses, and the resulting failure of the commuting identities and dependent interpolation estimates.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the invalid node-space estimate: v in H^s supplies only gradient regularity H^{s-1}, while applying the degree-(m-1) edge estimate yields h^{s-1}|gradient v|_{s-1}, not the stated h^s|gradient v|_s. Both also recognize the resulting undefined bound and overstatement of approximation order and give the regularity-consistent repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The node interpolation theorem applies an edge estimate to the gradient with the wrong regularity exponent and order, asserting an H^s gradient seminorm and h^s rate when the available estimate is based on H^{s-1} gradient regularity and an h^{s-1} rate.

component_coverage.gold_component: The stated regularity and degree mapping provide only gradient regularity one order lower, so the claimed h^s gradient estimate is undefined or false and must be replaced by the h^{s-1} regularity-consistent estimate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 states both the missing derivative/undefined seminorm problem and the one-order loss obtained by applying the edge estimate to the gradient, and proposes exactly the weakened estimate or an additional-derivative hypothesis.
